content.title: About
content.content: Croaker (*Sciaenidae*) is a marine fish found in coastal waters of the Pacific and Atlantic oceans. It has an elongated body covered with fine scales and produces a characteristic “drumming” sound by contracting muscles around its swim bladder.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Croaker belongs to the Sciaenidae family, which also includes drum and sea bass species.
The sound it produces is used in courtship rituals and territorial displays.
The fish can change its coloration depending on environment and stress level.
Croaker is widely used in Asian cuisines, especially in Japan and China.
In some regions it is considered an indicator of water quality because of its sensitivity to pollution.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Croaker provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: It contains EPA and DHA, which support heart and brain health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Rich in B12, B6 and niacin, which aid normal metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Provides selenium, iodine and phosphorus, important for thyroid function and bone health.

items.title: Low mercury levels
items.content: Compared with larger predatory fish, croaker typically has lower mercury, making it safer for regular consumption.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to seafood, including croaker.

items.title: Water contamination
items.content: Fish caught in polluted areas can contain heavy metals and microplastics.

items.title: Parasites
items.content: As with any raw fish, there is a risk of parasites; proper cooking eliminates this hazard.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Croaker can be pan‑fried, baked, steamed, or used in soups and stews. Fillets without bones are convenient for quick meals, while whole fish is often marinated with soy sauce and ginger before grilling.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Fresh croaker should be kept in the refrigerator at 0‑2 °C and used within 2 days. For longer storage, freeze the fish in an airtight bag at –18 °C; thaw in the refrigerator before cooking.
